mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate reduces the cost of capital for corporations, increasing the present value of future cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring additional conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below its 12-month moving average, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 5.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.5, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), rising prices erode corporate profit margins and prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.0, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) signals a robust labor market, supporting consumer spending and corporate earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days without requiring additional conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in less than 40% of periods when PAYEMS increases, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 115.0 indicates a manufacturing slowdown, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate output and potential earnings revisions.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 115.0, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in annualized GDP growth (GDPC1) and year-over-year housing starts (HOUST) signals a severe demand contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the market anticipates reduced corporate revenue.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening regime (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), higher interest rates reduce corporate borrowing and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.
